chapter_theme: Not killing (கொல்லாமை) is the finest offering in worship, and those who order killing are dragged to hell.
structure_note: Two verses: the first puts not killing at the head of inner worship, the second gives the punishment of those who urge killing.

197.reading: In worship of the good guru one clings to, among the many flowers the bright one is not killing other small lives; with it go the good garland, the unwavering lamp and the mind, and the place where the life settles is the crown of the head.
197.nuance: The verse turns the items of ritual worship (flower, garland, lamp) into inner ones, with not killing as the flower. அணுக்கள் may be small creatures or, in Siddhanta usage, souls. உச்சி is traditionally taken as the crown of the head where the yogi's awareness rests; a plainer reading of the last line isn't clear to me.

198.reading: Those brutish people who urged 'kill! stab!' are bound with strong ropes by Death's mighty servants, driven on with 'go! stop!', and made to stand in fire-mouthed hell.
198.nuance: The guilt falls on those who said 'kill' (கூறிய மாக்களை), not only on those who struck; the commands of the guilty are echoed back to them by Yama's servants ('go', 'stop', 'stay').

links.note: Both rank not killing above ritual offering: the Kural above a thousand oblations of ghee, Tirumular as the brightest of the flowers of worship.

Both say killing is paid for after this life, but differently: the Kural through rebirth in a wretched, diseased body, Tirumular through hell; and Tirumular extends the guilt to those who only urged the killing.
